# ParticleEmitter

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")`

Emits particles for effects such as sparks, smoke, dust and magic. Parent it to a `BasePart` or an `Attachment`: particles appear at its position and move along its up direction.

Particles are visual only. They collide with nothing, a script cannot find one, and they are simulated every frame instead of every tick. In return, a scene can hold thousands of them in one draw call.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Acceleration` | `vector` | `vector.create(0, 0, 0)` | read/write | A constant acceleration applied to every particle, in meters per second squared, in world space. `vector.create(0, -9.81, 0)` is gravity; a small upward value suits rising heat. |
| `Bounce` | `number` | `0.5` | read/write | The fraction of its speed into a surface that a particle keeps when it bounces, from 0 (none) to 1 (all). A particle that bounces too slowly to be seen comes to rest. |
| `Brightness` | `number` | `1` | read/write | A multiplier on the particle's color. It is not clamped; a value above 1 makes a particle bright enough to bloom. |
| `Collision` | `Enum.ParticleCollision` | `Enum.ParticleCollision.None` | read/write | What the particles collide with: nothing, the surfaces on screen, the terrain, or both. |
| `CollisionRadius` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The distance from a particle's center at which it collides, in meters. At 0, half the particle's size is used. |
| `CollisionResponse` | `Enum.ParticleCollisionResponse` | `Enum.ParticleCollisionResponse.Bounce` | read/write | What a particle does when it hits something: bounce, stick or die. |
| `Color` | `Color3` | `Color3.new(1, 1, 1)` | read/write | The color of a particle when it is emitted. |
| `ColorEnd` | `Color3` | `Color3.new(1, 1, 1)` | read/write | The color of a particle at the end of its life. The color changes gradually from `Color` to this. |
| `ColorOverLife` | `ColorSequence` | `ColorSequence.new(Color3.new(1, 1, 1))` | read/write | A color over a particle's life, from 0 when it is emitted to 1 when it dies. It is multiplied by the color that `Color` and `ColorEnd` give. White changes nothing. |
| `Drag` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The fraction of its velocity a particle loses each second. Use it for smoke, which slows; leave it at 0 for sparks. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the emitter emits continuously. `Emit` works whether it is on or off. |
| `FlipbookColumns` | `number` | `1` | read/write | The number of frames across `Texture`, from 1 to 16. Frames are read left to right, then top to bottom. |
| `FlipbookFramerate` | `number` | `12` | read/write | The speed of the flipbook animation, in frames per second, when `FlipbookMode` is `Loop`. |
| `FlipbookMode` | `Enum.ParticleFlipbookMode` | `Enum.ParticleFlipbookMode.Loop` | read/write | How a particle plays the frames of the flipbook: in a loop, once over its life, or as one still frame chosen for that particle. |
| `FlipbookRows` | `number` | `1` | read/write | The number of rows of frames in `Texture`, from 1 to 16. |
| `Friction` | `number` | `0.2` | read/write | The fraction of its speed along a surface that a particle loses each time it touches, from 0 (it slides forever) to 1 (it stops where it lands). |
| `Lifetime` | `number` | `2` | read/write | How long each particle lives, in seconds. |
| `LightEmission` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How much a particle adds its light to what is behind it instead of covering it, from 0 to 1. At 0 it is blended over the background. At 1 it is added to it and never darkens anything, which suits fire, sparks and magic. |
| `LightInfluence` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How much the scene's light decides a particle's color, from 0 to 1. At 0 it is always its own color. At 1 it is lit by the sky and the sun, and darker in the shadows things cast, as smoke and dust are. The light a particle adds (`LightEmission`) is its own at any value. |
| `Rate` | `number` | `20` | read/write | The number of particles emitted per second while the emitter is enabled. |
| `Rotation` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The angle, in degrees, a particle is rotated by when it is emitted, in the plane facing the camera. |
| `RotationSpeed` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How fast a particle rotates, in degrees per second. A negative value rotates the other way. |
| `RotationSpeedSpread` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The largest random amount, in degrees per second, added to or subtracted from `RotationSpeed` for each particle. |
| `RotationSpread` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The largest random angle, in degrees, added to or subtracted from `Rotation` for each particle. At 180, particles are emitted at any angle. |
| `Shape` | `Enum.ParticleShape` | `Enum.ParticleShape.Soft` | read/write | The shape a particle is drawn as when the emitter has no `Texture`. |
| `Simulation` | `Enum.ParticleSimulation` | `Enum.ParticleSimulation.Cpu` | read/write | Whether the particles are simulated on the CPU or on the GPU. The GPU handles a hundred thousand particles where the CPU handles a few thousand. A machine without compute shaders always simulates on the CPU, and logs a message once. |
| `Size` | `number` | `0.5` | read/write | The width of a particle when it is emitted, in meters. |
| `SizeEnd` | `number` | `0.5` | read/write | The width of a particle at the end of its life, in meters. |
| `SizeOverLife` | `NumberSequence` | `NumberSequence.new(1)` | read/write | A scale over a particle's life, multiplied by the size that `Size` and `SizeEnd` give. For a puff that swells and shrinks, use a curve that rises and falls. A value of 1 changes nothing. |
| `Speed` | `number` | `4` | read/write | The speed of a particle when it is emitted, in meters per second, along the emitter's up direction. |
| `SpreadAngle` | `number` | `15` | read/write | The largest angle, in degrees, between a particle's direction and the emitter's up direction. 0 is a jet and 180 is a sphere. |
| `Texture` | `Content` | — | read/write | The image each particle is drawn as, facing the camera. Its color is multiplied by the particle's color, and its alpha channel gives the particle's outline. With no texture, `Shape` is drawn. With `FlipbookColumns` or `FlipbookRows` above 1, the image is a grid of animation frames. |
| `Transparency` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How transparent a particle is when it is emitted, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible). |
| `TransparencyEnd` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How transparent a particle is at the end of its life, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible). With the default, each particle fades out as it dies. |
| `TransparencyOverLife` | `NumberSequence` | `NumberSequence.new(0)` | read/write | A transparency over a particle's life, combined with the one that `Transparency` and `TransparencyEnd` give, like one transparent layer over another. For a fade in and out, use a curve from 1 down to 0 and back to 1. A value of 0 changes nothing. |
| `WindAffectsDrift` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the workspace's wind carries the particles. The wind at each particle's position is added to its motion. Off by default. |

## Methods

### `Emit(count: number)`

Emits `count` particles at once, whether or not the emitter is enabled. Use it for a burst such as an explosion. One call emits at most 1,000.
